name: Daylight (DaylightRx)
one_liner: Self-guided digital CBT app for generalized anxiety and worry from Big Health; FDA-cleared as DaylightRx and offered by prescription or employer.
best_for: Adults with ongoing worry or generalized anxiety who want structured CBT on their phone
People whose employer or health plan offers Daylight
Adults 22+ whose clinician can prescribe DaylightRx, including Medicare patients
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People without a prescription or a sponsoring employer or plan: there is no self-pay option
People who need a live therapist or medication
short_description: Daylight is an app-based CBT program for generalized anxiety; DaylightRx is the FDA-cleared prescription version.
long_description: Daylight, from Big Health, is a self-guided smartphone program that teaches cognitive behavioral therapy skills for worry and generalized anxiety through short voice-guided, animated sessions and practice techniques. DaylightRx, the prescription version, received FDA 510(k) clearance in 2024 for adults 22 and older with generalized anxiety disorder, as an add-on to usual care; Medicare billing codes have existed since January 2025. The non-prescription Daylight app is available only to people with an account through an employer or health plan. Two Big Health-funded randomized trials found larger anxiety reductions than a waitlist and than psychoeducation.
patient_summary: Daylight teaches you CBT skills for worry and anxiety through short guided sessions on your phone. You can get it through a clinician's prescription (DaylightRx) or free if your employer or health plan offers it. There is no way to buy it yourself.

pricing.starting_price: Free through some employers; copay with insurance or Medicare by prescription
pricing.notes: No self-pay price published. Medicare codes since January 2025; commercial coverage varies and you may owe a cost share.

privacy.notes: Big Health privacy notice (read 2026-10-27) says it may 'sell' or 'share' data via advertising cookies and pixels on its corporate website and lets ad partners collect identifiers and activity data for interest-based ads; deletion requests offered to all users regardless of location.

faqs.q: Is Daylight app effective for anxiety?
faqs.a: Yes, randomized controlled trials show 71% of Daylight users achieve clinically meaningful anxiety reduction. The app delivers CBT—the evidence-based treatment recommended by clinical guidelines. It's more structured than relaxation apps, teaching skills to manage anxiety long-term.

Daylight is free if your employer or health plan covers it. Check with HR or your insurance benefits portal. Like Sleepio, Daylight isn't available for individual purchase—access is through employer or insurance partnerships.

faqs.q: How is Daylight different from Calm or Headspace?
faqs.a: Daylight delivers structured CBT treatment—cognitive restructuring, worry management, and behavioral techniques. Calm and Headspace focus on relaxation and mindfulness. If you have clinical anxiety, Daylight's therapeutic approach addresses root causes rather than just symptoms.

For mild-moderate generalized anxiety, Daylight provides CBT comparable to some therapy outcomes. For severe anxiety, complex trauma, or other conditions, Daylight works best alongside professional care. Talk to a provider if symptoms are significantly impacting your life.
